proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a one-stratum law and suppress the stratum subscript.  The overlap condition in \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\) gives \(0<e_x<1\).  Let \(Q\in\mathcal H_\Gamma(P)\), and set
\[
s_{ij}=Q\{Y(0)=i,Y(1)=j\},
\qquad
q_{ij}=Q\{Z=1\mid Y(0)=i,Y(1)=j\}
\]
on every positive-mass response type.  By \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\mbox{-}class}\),
\[
0<\ell_x\leq q_{ij}\leq u_x<1
\tag{1}
\]
whenever \(s_{ij}>0\), and consistency identifies \(Y\) with \(Y(1)\) when \(Z=1\) and with \(Y(0)\) when \(Z=0\).

Choose arbitrary versions within the declared boxes for the conditional expectations defining \(w_Q\) on null observed cells.  On positive observed cells, finite iterated summation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
e_xE_P\{w_Q(Y,1)\mid Z=1\}
&=E_Q\{Z w_Q(Y(1),1)\}\\
&=E_Q\!\left\{\frac{Z}{q_{Y(0),Y(1)}}\right\}
=\sum_{i,j:s_{ij}>0}s_{ij}q_{ij}\frac{1}{q_{ij}}=1,
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
and similarly
\[
(1-e_x)E_P\{w_Q(Y,0)\mid Z=0\}
=E_Q\!\left\{\frac{1-Z}{1-q_{Y(0),Y(1)}}\right\}=1.
\tag{3}
\]
Because conditional averaging preserves intervals, (1) implies
\[
e_xw_Q(y,1)\in[e_x/u_x,e_x/\ell_x],
\qquad
(1-e_x)w_Q(y,0)
\in[(1-e_x)/(1-\ell_x),(1-e_x)/(1-u_x)].
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (2)--(4) are exactly the normalization and box restrictions in the current definition \(\mathrm{def{:}ihk\mbox{-}jensen\mbox{-}cmc\mbox{-}program}\).  Thus
\[
w_Q\in\mathcal W^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\Gamma(P).
\tag{5}
\]
This proves only a map into the note-defined box-augmented specialization; no reverse realizability assertion is made.

The same cancellation and the consistency restriction give
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P\{Zw_Q(Y,1)Y\}
&=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}q_{ij}\frac{j}{q_{ij}}
=E_Q\{Y(1)\},\\
E_P\{(1-Z)w_Q(Y,0)Y\}
&=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}(1-q_{ij})\frac{i}{1-q_{ij}}
=E_Q\{Y(0)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
Hence \(T(Q)=\tau\) implies that \(w_Q\) satisfies the ATE equality in \(\mathrm{def{:}ihk\mbox{-}jensen\mbox{-}cmc\mbox{-}program}\) at the same \(\tau\).

We next compare the two costs.  The response-type definitions give \(a_{ij}=s_{ij}q_{ij}\), \(b_{ij}=s_{ij}(1-q_{ij})\), and therefore
\[
d_{ij}=(1-e_x)a_{ij}-e_xb_{ij}=s_{ij}(q_{ij}-e_x).
\tag{7}
\]
The closed-perspective formula in \(\mathrm{def{:}assignment\mbox{-}cost}\) consequently becomes
\[
R_P(Q)=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}\frac{(q_{ij}-e_x)^2}{e_x(1-e_x)},
\tag{8}
\]
where a zero-mass type contributes zero.  For the observed-policy-first orientation and \(f_N(r)=r^{-1}-1\), direct algebra on each positive-mass type gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&q_{ij}f_N(e_x/q_{ij})
+(1-q_{ij})f_N((1-e_x)/(1-q_{ij}))\\
&\qquad=\frac{q_{ij}^2}{e_x}
+\frac{(1-q_{ij})^2}{1-e_x}-1
=\frac{(q_{ij}-e_x)^2}{e_x(1-e_x)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Thus the corresponding unrelaxed latent-law divergence equals (8) exactly.

It remains to verify the Jensen contraction used by the exact displayed program.  For a finite probability vector \((\lambda_k)_k\), positive numbers \((r_k)_k\), and \(S=\sum_k\lambda_kr_k\), expansion and pairing of the \((k,l)\) and \((l,k)\) terms yields
\[
\sum_k\lambda_k f_N(r_k)-f_N(S)
=\frac{1}{S}\sum_{k<l}\lambda_k\lambda_l
\frac{(r_k-r_l)^2}{r_kr_l}\geq0.
\tag{10}
\]
Apply (10) separately within each positive observed \((Y,Z)\) cell, taking \(r=e_x/q_{ij}\) in a treated cell and \(r=(1-e_x)/(1-q_{ij})\) in a control cell.  By the definition of \(w_Q\), the respective cell averages of \(r\) are \(e_xw_Q(y,1)\) and \((1-e_x)w_Q(y,0)\).  Multiplication by the observed cell probabilities, summation over the cells, and (8)--(9) then give
\[
\mathscr R_{\mathrm{IHK},P}(w_Q)\leq R_P(Q).
\tag{11}
\]
Together, (5), (6), and (11) establish the asserted one-way, ATE-preserving, cost-nonincreasing embedding.  If the full-law ATE fiber is nonempty, taking infima in (11) gives
\[
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_P(\tau)\leq C_P(\tau);
\tag{12}
\]
if it is empty, the right side is \(+\infty\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}frontier}\), so (12) still holds in the extended-real order.

For completeness, consider the budget statement for the relaxed program.  Delete weight coordinates attached to null observed cells, which affect neither its constraints nor its objective.  Every remaining normalized coordinate \(e_xw(y,1)\) or \((1-e_x)w(y,0)\) lies in a closed bounded interval with a strictly positive lower endpoint by (1) and (4).  The two normalization equations and the ATE equation are closed affine restrictions.  Therefore any nonempty ATE slice is compact.  Since \(f_N\) is continuous on those positive boxes, a minimizing sequence has a convergent subsequence whose limit is feasible and attains the infimum.  If the slice is empty its infimum is \(+\infty\).  Hence the relaxed slice contains a weight of cost at most \(\rho\) if and only if \(\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_P(\tau)\leq\rho\).  The corresponding full-law attainment and budget equivalence follow from the already established \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\); (5)--(12) supply the same-budget implication into the relaxed specialization.

Now take \(e_x=1/2\), \(p_1=4/5\), \(p_0=1/5\), \(\Gamma=4\), and \(\tau=3/10\).  For a feasible weight define
\[
r_1(y)=e_xw(y,1),\qquad r_0(y)=(1-e_x)w(y,0),
\]
and let \(m_z\) be the mean of \(Y\) under the normalized reweighting in arm \(z\).  Binary support and the two normalizations are equivalent to
\[
r_1(1)=\frac{m_1}{p_1},\quad
r_1(0)=\frac{1-m_1}{1-p_1},\qquad
r_0(1)=\frac{m_0}{p_0},\quad
r_0(0)=\frac{1-m_0}{1-p_0}.
\tag{13}
\]
For \(p,m\in(0,1)\), substitution into the armwise Neyman objective gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
pf_N(m/p)+(1-p)f_N((1-m)/(1-p))
&=\frac{p^2}{m}+\frac{(1-p)^2}{1-m}-1\\
&=\frac{(m-p)^2}{m(1-m)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
Because both treatment-arm probabilities equal \(1/2\), the exact objective in \(\mathrm{def{:}ihk\mbox{-}jensen\mbox{-}cmc\mbox{-}program}\) is therefore
\[
J(m_1,m_0)
=\frac12\frac{(m_1-4/5)^2}{m_1(1-m_1)}
+\frac12\frac{(m_0-1/5)^2}{m_0(1-m_0)},
\tag{15}
\]
and its ATE equality is \(m_1-m_0=3/10\).

Here \(\ell_x=1/5\) and \(u_x=4/5\), so both normalized-weight boxes in the current definition are \([5/8,5/2]\).  Applying this box to all four coordinates in (13) is equivalent to
\[
m_1\in[1/2,7/8],\qquad m_0\in[1/8,1/2].
\tag{16}
\]
Writing \(m_0=x\) and \(m_1=x+3/10\), the exact feasible ATE slice in (16) is \(x\in[1/5,1/2]\).

For \(g_p(m)=(m-p)^2/\{m(1-m)\}\), the representation in (14) yields
\[
g_p''(m)=\frac{2p^2}{m^3}+\frac{2(1-p)^2}{(1-m)^3}>0.
\tag{17}
\]
Thus the sliced objective is strictly convex.  The identity \(g_{4/5}(m)=g_{1/5}(1-m)\) makes its derivative vanish at
\[
(m_1,m_0)=(13/20,7/20),
\tag{18}
\]
which lies in the relative interior of (16), so it is the unique minimizer.  Evaluation gives
\[
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_P(3/10)
=J(13/20,7/20)
=\frac{(3/20)^2}{(13/20)(7/20)}
=\frac9{91}.
\tag{19}
\]
By the already established \(\mathrm{thm{:}symmetric\mbox{-}family}\), the same observed law and odds cap satisfy
\[
C_P(3/10)
=\frac{(3/5-3/10)^2}{1-3/10}
=\frac9{70}.
\tag{20}
\]
Consequently
\[
C_P(3/10)-\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_P(3/10)
=\frac9{70}-\frac9{91}
=\frac{27}{910}>0.
\tag{21}
\]
This proves the exact strict separation for the current box-augmented program and completes the proof.

Parameterize a one-stratum binary observed law by
\[
\theta=(e,p_1,p_0)\in(0,1)^3,
\]
where \(e=e_x\).  Its four observable probabilities, in the order \((Z,Y)=(1,1),(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)\), are
\[
ep_1,\qquad e(1-p_1),\qquad(1-e)p_0,\qquad(1-e)(1-p_0).
\tag{22}
\]
On the positive-cell region the inverse coordinates are
\[
e=P(Z=1),\qquad
p_1=\frac{P(Z=1,Y=1)}{P(Z=1)},\qquad
p_0=\frac{P(Z=0,Y=1)}{P(Z=0)}.
\tag{23}
\]
Thus \(\theta\) is a homeomorphic coordinate system on the interior of the one-stratum observed-law simplex.  Put
\[
\theta_\star=(1/2,4/5,1/5),
\qquad \tau_\star=3/10.
\]
Write \(C_\theta\) and \(\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\theta\) for the two frontiers at the law indexed by \(\theta\).  The proved \(\mathrm{thm{:}strict\mbox{-}jensen\mbox{-}gap}\) gives
\[
C_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star)=\frac9{70},\qquad
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star)=\frac9{91},\qquad
g_\star:=\frac9{70}-\frac9{91}=\frac{27}{910}.
\tag{24}
\]

We first prove continuity of the full-law value at \(\theta_\star\), without assuming that an odds face remains active.  At \(\tau=\tau_\star\) and \(\Gamma=4\), write
\[
A_\theta=e(1-p_1),\qquad
B_\theta=(1-e)p_0,
\qquad
D_\theta=1-ep_1-(1-e)p_0,
\]
and evaluate the formulas in \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\mbox{-}scalar\mbox{-}program}\) at these quantities.  At \(\theta_\star\),
\[
A_{\theta_\star}=B_{\theta_\star}=\frac1{10},
\qquad D_{\theta_\star}=\frac12,
\qquad \ell=\frac15,
\qquad u=\frac45.
\]
The three lower-face values are \(1/8,1/5,13/50\), and the three upper-face values are \(1/2,23/40,11/25\).  Hence
\[
[L_{\theta_\star},U_{\theta_\star}]=[13/50,11/25].
\tag{25}
\]
The point \(v_\star=7/20\) is at distance \(9/100\) from both endpoints, and direct substitution gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_{\theta_\star}(v_\star)
&=4\left(\frac1{35}+\frac5{28}+\frac3{40}-\frac14\right)\\
&=\frac9{70}=C_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star),
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]
where the last equality is (24).

Each candidate face defining \(L_\theta\) and \(U_\theta\) is continuous at \(\theta_\star\), because \(e\in(0,1)\) implies \(0<\ell(e)<u(e)<1\); a finite maximum or minimum preserves continuity.  Hence, on a neighborhood of \(\theta_\star\), \(v_\star\) remains feasible and all feasible intervals lie in a common compact interval on which \(v\), \(1-\tau_\star-v\), \(e\), and \(1-e\) are bounded away from zero.  The displayed formula for \(F_\tau\) is jointly continuous there.

Let \(\theta_n\to\theta_\star\).  Feasibility of \(v_\star\), (26), and the exact scalar characterization in the already established \(\mathrm{thm{:}binary\mbox{-}phase\mbox{-}catalog}\) give
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}C_{\theta_n}(\tau_\star)
\leq\lim_{n\to\infty}F_{\theta_n}(v_\star)
=C_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star).
\tag{27}
\]
For all large \(n\), choose a minimizer \(v_n\in[L_{\theta_n},U_{\theta_n}]\), whose existence follows from continuity on the compact scalar interval.  Along a subsequence realizing the lower limit, compactness supplies a further subsequence with \(v_n\to v\).  Continuity of both endpoints implies \(v\in[L_{\theta_\star},U_{\theta_\star}]\), and joint continuity yields
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}C_{\theta_n}(\tau_\star)
=F_{\theta_\star}(v)
\geq C_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star).
\tag{28}
\]
Equations (27)--(28) prove continuity of \(C_\theta(\tau_\star)\) at \(\theta_\star\).

We next prove continuity of the value of the exact current box-augmented program.  Put \(r_1=ew(\,\cdot\,,1)\) and \(r_0=(1-e)w(\,\cdot\,,0)\).  When \(\Gamma=4\), substitution into the odds faces in \(\mathrm{def{:}ihk\mbox{-}jensen\mbox{-}cmc\mbox{-}program}\) gives
\[
a_1(e)=\frac{1+3e}{4},\quad b_1(e)=4-3e,
\qquad
a_0(e)=\frac{4-3e}{4},\quad b_0(e)=1+3e
\tag{29}
\]
as the lower and upper endpoints for \(r_1\) and \(r_0\), respectively.  With \(p_z=p_1\) for \(z=1\) and \(p_z=p_0\) for \(z=0\), define
\[
\lambda_z(\theta)
=\max\{a_z(e)p_z,\,1-b_z(e)(1-p_z)\},
\qquad
\nu_z(\theta)
=\min\{b_z(e)p_z,\,1-a_z(e)(1-p_z)\}.
\tag{30}
\]
If \(m_z\) is the normalized reweighted mean in arm \(z\), binary support and normalization force, and are forced by,
\[
r_z(1)=m_z/p_z,
\qquad r_z(0)=(1-m_z)/(1-p_z).
\tag{31}
\]
Applying both box inequalities in (29) to both coordinates in (31) proves in both directions that the attainable means are exactly
\[
m_z\in[\lambda_z(\theta),\nu_z(\theta)].
\tag{32}
\]
Writing \(x=m_0\) and \(m_1=x+\tau_\star\), the relaxed ATE slice is therefore exactly
\[
\widetilde L_\theta
:=\max\{\lambda_0(\theta),\lambda_1(\theta)-\tau_\star\}
\leq x\leq
\min\{\nu_0(\theta),\nu_1(\theta)-\tau_\star\}
=:\widetilde U_\theta.
\tag{33}
\]
The algebra in equation (14) of the proof of \(\mathrm{thm{:}strict\mbox{-}jensen\mbox{-}gap}\), now weighted by the observed arm probabilities appearing in the exact definition, makes the sliced objective
\[
\widetilde F_\theta(x)
=e\,g_{p_1}(x+\tau_\star)+(1-e)g_{p_0}(x),
\qquad
g_p(m)=\frac{(m-p)^2}{m(1-m)}.
\tag{34}
\]
At \(\theta_\star\), equations (29)--(33) give
\[
[\widetilde L_{\theta_\star},\widetilde U_{\theta_\star}]=[1/5,1/2].
\tag{35}
\]
The minimizer \(x_\star=7/20\) established in \(\mathrm{thm{:}strict\mbox{-}jensen\mbox{-}gap}\) is at distance \(3/20\) from both endpoints and satisfies
\[
\widetilde F_{\theta_\star}(x_\star)
=\frac9{91}
=\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star).
\tag{36}
\]
All endpoints in (33) are continuous by (29)--(30).  Near (35), the quantities \(x\), \(1-x\), \(x+\tau_\star\), and \(1-x-\tau_\star\) are uniformly positive, so (34) is jointly continuous on a common compact interval.  Repeating the subsequence argument in (27)--(28), now using the strictly feasible point \(x_\star\) for the upper limit and minimizers in (33) for the lower limit, proves
\[
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\theta(\tau_\star)
\longrightarrow
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star)
\quad\text{as }\theta\to\theta_\star.
\tag{37}
\]

By (24), (27)--(28), and (37), there is \(\eta_0>0\) such that throughout the strict cube
\[
B_{\eta_0}:=\{\theta:\|\theta-\theta_\star\|_\infty<\eta_0\}
\]
both scalar intervals are nonempty and
\[
\left|C_\theta(\tau_\star)-\frac9{70}\right|<\frac{g_\star}{4},
\qquad
\left|\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\theta(\tau_\star)-\frac9{91}\right|<\frac{g_\star}{4}.
\tag{38}
\]
Choose
\[
0<\eta\leq\min\{\eta_0,1/10\}.
\tag{39}
\]
For every \(\theta\in B_\eta\),
\[
\begin{gathered}
 e\geq\frac12-\eta,\qquad 1-e\geq\frac12-\eta,\\
p_1\geq\frac45-\eta,\qquad 1-p_1\geq\frac15-\eta,\\
p_0\geq\frac15-\eta,\qquad 1-p_0\geq\frac45-\eta.
\end{gathered}
\tag{40}
\]
Equations (22) and (40) therefore give the explicit common support bound
\[
P(Z=z,Y=y)
\geq\left(\frac12-\eta\right)
       \left(\frac15-\eta\right)>0
\qquad(z,y\in\{0,1\}).
\tag{41}
\]
The conditional arm variances and treatment variance similarly satisfy
\[
p_z(1-p_z)
\geq\left(\frac15-\eta\right)
       \left(\frac45-\eta\right)>0
\quad(z=0,1),
\qquad
e(1-e)\geq\left(\frac12-\eta\right)^2>0.
\tag{42}
\]
Thus this neighborhood is uniformly separated from every observable support boundary relevant to either scalar program.

The cube \(B_\eta\) is nonempty and has three-dimensional Lebesgue volume \((2\eta)^3>0\).  For the map from \(\theta\) to the first three cell probabilities in (22), direct differentiation gives the absolute Jacobian determinant
\[
e(1-e)\geq\left(\frac12-\eta\right)^2>0.
\tag{43}
\]
Together with the continuous inverse (23), this shows that the image of \(B_\eta\) is a nonempty open Euclidean neighborhood in the interior of the observed-law simplex.  It contains a Euclidean ball and consequently has positive three-dimensional volume; it is not a lower-dimensional path or face.

Finally, subtracting the two inequalities in (38) and using (24) yields, for every \(\theta\in B_\eta\),
\[
C_\theta(3/10)-\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\theta(3/10)
\geq g_\star-\frac{g_\star}{2}
=\frac{27}{1820}>0.
\tag{44}
\]
The preserved strictly feasible points \(v_\star\) and \(x_\star\) prove that both values are finite throughout this neighborhood.  Equations (39)--(44) prove the asserted locally uniform strict separation, the positive support bounds, and the positive-volume claim.

prose_updates.tldr: A finite observed law is lifted to one joint law of treatment and both potential outcomes, and the least Pearson assignment information needed to support each ATE is profiled. The attained sharp frontier has a perspective SOCP and explicit dual. For binary outcomes, a treatment-independent garbling removes the minority discordant response type without imposing monotone treatment response and without increasing any convex assignment cost; this yields the complete six-face scalar catalog and a squared-correlation null identity. A one-way, cost-nonincreasing embedding into the explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of Ishikawa--He--Kanamori equation~(14) gives the exact separation \(9/70>9/91\); strict interiority and continuity extend it to a nonempty open neighborhood with a uniformly positive gap. On a named uniformly Slater-regular multinomial region, a fixed-odds-cone parametrization, a uniform equality right inverse, and bounded attained cellwise dual multipliers yield a finite-sample \(O(n^{-1/2})\) profile diameter without transporting a dual certificate between laws; a contiguous boundary pair shows that honest bands must retain infinite diameter at a finite-to-infinite null-cost boundary.

project_justification.gap: Average-case sensitivity analysis has sharp armwise potential-outcome bounds but no jointly attained ATE frontier. Ishikawa--He--Kanamori's equations~(10), (12), and (14) provide an observed-policy-first divergence and Jensen--CMC computation, but the resulting armwise weights need not be realizable by one cross-world-compatible assignment law. Existing work therefore neither supplies the one-way full-law embedding on the same Neyman budget scale nor establishes an exact and open-set strict cost gap. Existing inference theory also does not quantify both the regular finite-sample width and the finite-to-infinite boundary obstruction for this frontier.
project_justification.niche: Finite outcomes make the missing joint law explicit, expose a response-type garbling geometry invisible to armwise reweighting, and permit an interior finite-dimensional comparison showing that the relaxation gap is robust to small changes in the observed law.
project_justification.fill: The project profiles the exact full-law Pearson cost, certifies it by primal and dual conic programs, solves the binary geometry, and maps each compatible full law one way into an explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of Ishikawa--He--Kanamori equation~(14) at no greater cost. It proves the exact values \(9/70\) and \(9/91\) and, by continuity at strictly interior scalar minimizers, a uniformly positive gap on a nonempty open neighborhood. It also pairs a finite-sample regular-region diameter theorem based on a common fixed odds cone and uniformly bounded attained multipliers with a contiguous boundary lower bound.

prose_updates.related_work: Rubin supplies the potential-outcome notation and consistency framework, while Tan supplies the marginal odds-ratio sensitivity model used for the assignment restriction. Zhang and Zhao motivate average rather than worst-case assignment distortion and prove sharp bounds for each average potential outcome, but their discussion explicitly withholds joint ATE attainment. Dorn and Guo's quantile-balancing result and Dorn, Guo, and Kallus's doubly sharp extension establish sharp worst-case marginal-sensitivity benchmarks; neither profiles one joint full-law average assignment budget. Ishikawa and He's kernel conditional-moment construction and Jin, Ren, and Zhou's general \(f\)-sensitivity model motivate tractable observed-weight relaxations, but do not impose the present cross-world-compatible joint response law. Ishikawa, He, and Kanamori define an observed-policy-first \(f\)-divergence in their equation~(10), apply Jensen in equation~(12), and combine the relaxed divergence with CMC in equation~(14). The comparison here is deliberately one way: every compatible full law induces a feasible point of the note's explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization with no larger cost; no equality with their unqualified published class and no reverse cross-world realizability are claimed. The rational witness has values \(9/70\) and \(9/91\), and strict interiority of both scalar programs makes the gap uniformly positive on an open neighborhood of observed laws. Balke and Pearl supply the finite response-type representation, and Manski supplies the substantive monotone-response benchmark; the binary garbling result instead derives monotone support for an extremal compatible law without assuming monotone treatment response of the population. Blackwell's comparison-of-experiments order motivates the garbling language, but does not establish preservation of the two observed causal margins and ATE proved here. The regular finite-sample theorem rescales response-type masses onto a common odds cone, derives a uniform right inverse and multiplier bound from the declared Slater margin, and compares different observed laws through the saddle identity at each law rather than reusing a moved dual certificate. Duan, Zhang, and Zhang derive directional derivatives for finite-valued Slater-regular SOCP values, while Duchi, Glynn, and Namkoong study generalized empirical-likelihood robust optimization; neither covers this support-changing extended-real profile. Fang and Santos, Firpo, Galvao, and Parker, and Masten and Poirier provide directional or breakdown-frontier inference tools, while Zhao, Small, and Bhattacharya give a bootstrap sensitivity procedure; extending such inference through this frontier's zero cells and moving faces remains open. Masten, Poirier, and Ren provide a general relaxation-of-unconfoundedness perspective, whereas the present result specializes to an attained finite full-law information frontier. Nattino, Ashmead, and Lu motivate the undeveloped complex-survey extension, and Cinelli and Hazlett motivate observed-covariate calibration; neither extension or empirical application is claimed here.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The sharpness, dual attainment, garbling, scalar catalog, one-way cost transfer into the explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization, exact rational separation, open-neighborhood uniform gap, regular-region finite-sample diameter, and boundary impossibility are theorem claims proved in the note. The comparison does not identify that specialization with Ishikawa--He--Kanamori's unqualified published class and does not assert that every relaxed armwise weight is induced by a compatible cross-world assignment law. The regular diameter proof controls coefficient movement through a common fixed odds cone and a law-specific saddle comparison; it does not claim stability of an active set or feasibility of one law's dual certificate at another law. Uniform tangent inference under weaker facial regularity and adaptive derivative-bootstrap inversion remain open. The \(\Gamma=1\) specialization is retained only as a regression corollary. The application target remains a prespecified categorical mercury score and finite covariate stratification; it does not claim to recover the original continuous-outcome NHANES estimand.

statement_notes.justification: The explicit inverse-propensity map proves a one-way inclusion and same-scale cost transfer from compatible full laws into the explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization, while the exact rational witness quantifies the price of requiring one cross-world-compatible assignment mechanism.
statement_notes.gap: IshikawaHeKanamori2026Convex, equations~(10), (12), and (14), defines the unrelaxed \(f\)-divergence and its Jensen--CMC relaxation, but does not prove reverse cross-world realizability, the Neyman-generator full-law embedding used here, or the strict \(9/70\) versus \(9/91\) full-law ATE gap.
statement_notes.consumer: A sensitivity analyst treats the relaxed program as a one-way lower-cost screen, not as an identical feasible-law class, and avoids declaring the ATE \(3/10\) feasible at budgets between \(9/91\) and \(9/70\) for the witness law.

statement_notes.justification: Strictly interior minimizers in both finite-dimensional scalar programs make the exact witness robust: continuity preserves at least half of its rational cost gap on a nonempty open neighborhood.
statement_notes.gap: A single numerical or rational witness could be a knife-edge phenomenon; the local theorem rules this out without assuming fixed active odds faces throughout the neighborhood.
statement_notes.consumer: The comparison remains informative under small multinomial sampling perturbations of the treated fraction and the two observed arm success probabilities.
